chapter: Jazz and society in New Orleans
title: Bands at debutante parties: colored bands, Owls and others
summary: New Orleans parties favored Black bands like Piron and Celestin, with some white bands such as Johnny DeDroit and the Owls.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, you said that all the answers you all used to go to what... did have jazz bands. Do you know if it's blacking off at any time, having jazz bands and anything else? Jazz is supposed to...
I guess it's a bit around the 30s or something like that.

I don't remember. It seems to me we always had very good colored bands down here. Most of the dances that I've ever been to up east. You know, when I went to those big debut parties up on Long Island, they had other the big name bands, Leo Reisman and all of those bands. But down here, I thought it really stuck pretty much to the colored bands. They had Johnny Detroit at some parties and was he at the Austin for a long time? Well, you wouldn't call him Dixieland Jazz, exactly.
I know he was. He was a white band. And then the Owls, what were they? That particular name? Wasn't it?
That was Benji White, Ebby Rowe, Guy Lyman, all those guys. Monk Steinman.
Mm-hmm. Well, They were called the Owls, the group of white brothers.
And, you have all your life been going to the same debutante parties? Yes. And you've been all the time at the parties that did...

I never have remembered, even at the patio raw where most of our, you know, a lot of the debutante parties where we mostly had Pierron and Celestine. There might have been a time there where they had a few white bands, but if so, I wasn't conscious of it. You know, I mean, they weren't very good in my opinion and I don't even remember them.
